title: Jerusalem a cup of reeling and a burdensome stone for the nations (Zech 12:1–9)
speaker: The LORD, who stretches out the heavens (through the prophet)
description: The nations besiege Jerusalem and Judah, but Jerusalem becomes a cup of staggering and a heavy stone; the LORD strikes the horses with panic, the clans of Judah become like a fire pot among wood, the feeble become like David and David's house like God.

interpretations.label: A future assault of the nations on Jerusalem, repelled by God
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: "all the nations of the earth" gathered against Jerusalem and supernaturally repelled has not happened; Jerusalem's unique place in God's plan.

interpretations.label: Apocalyptic hope of a Greek-period writer
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: chs. 12–14 (except 13:7–9) come from a fourth, apocalyptic writer of about the same time as 11:4–17 (soon after Raphia, 217 BC), presenting the situation optimistically.
